# CBAM compliance answer, v1

You answer questions about the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)
using only the retrieved context below. You are read by compliance staff who
will act on what you write, so an admission of missing information is more
useful than a plausible guess.

## Rules

1. Use only the context. Do not use background knowledge about CBAM, EU law or
   emissions trading, even if you are confident it is correct.
2. Cite every factual claim with the chunk id it came from, in square
   brackets, exactly as the id appears in the context: `[reg_2023_956#0007]`.
   A sentence may carry more than one citation.
3. If the context does not contain enough to answer, say exactly what is
   missing and stop. Do not answer partially and then hedge.
4. Quote the operative wording of an obligation (deadline, threshold, duty
   holder) rather than paraphrasing it.
5. No preamble, no restatement of the question, no closing summary. Answer in
   at most 200 words.

Article 3
Submission of the CBAM report
The reporting declarant shall submit the CBAM report through the CBAM
transitional registry no later than one month after the end of the quarter to
which it relates. A report shall be considered submitted when it has been
assigned a unique report identification number by the registry.

Article 4
Modification and correction of reports
The reporting declarant may modify a submitted CBAM report until two months
after the end of the relevant reporting quarter. By way of derogation, the
reporting declarant may modify the CBAM reports for the first two reporting
periods until the submission deadline of the third CBAM report. Beyond those
deadlines, the reporting declarant may request the competent authority to
correct a report within one

Article 5
Methods for determining embedded emissions

an emission monitoring scheme at the installation which can include verification
by an accredited verifier; or, for reports due for periods ending before 31 July
2024 only, estimated values published by the Commission for the transitional
period.

The reporting declarant shall request from the operator of the installation the
information listed in Annex I to this synthetic Implementing Regulation. Where
the operator does not provide that information, the reporting declarant shall
record the request and the absence of a response, and shall state in the CBAM
report which method was used instead.

11 Penalties during the transitional period
If you do not report, or you report something incomplete or incorrect and do not
fix it when asked, the penalty is between EUR 10 and EUR 50 per tonne of
unreported emissions. It goes up if you have submitted more than two bad reports
in a row or if you have not reported for more than six months. The authority
takes into account how much was missing, whether you cooperated, and whether it
was deliberate.

12 Common mistakes
Reporting electricity in tonnes rather than megawatt hours. Assuming the
estimated values published for the transitional period remain available after 31
July 2024. Assuming indirect emissions are reported for iron and steel during
the transitional period, when only direct emissions are. Forgetting that the
EUR 150 threshold is per consignment, not per year.

9 Carbon prices you already pay
If your emissions are subject to a carbon price where you are, tell the importer
the price due for the emissions concerned and whether any rebate or other
compensation is available on export. The importer can only claim a reduction
where the price was effectively paid and no export rebate was available.

10 What happens if you provide nothing
The importer records the request and the absence of a response, and falls back
to default values. Default values are set at the average emission intensity of
your country for that type of goods, increased by a mark-up. If reliable country
data is not available, they are based on the average of the ten worst performing
installations in the customs territory. Both are usually worse for you than your
actual figures.

3 What changes and when
From 1 October 2023 to 31 December 2025 you only report. You do not buy
certificates and you do not pay anything under the mechanism. From 1 January
2026 you must be an authorised declarant before you import, you submit an annual
declaration, and you surrender certificates for the emissions you declared.

4 Quarterly reporting during the transitional period
You submit one report per quarter through the transitional registry, within one
month of the quarter ending. So the report for January to March is due by 30
April. You report how much of each good you imported, where it was made, which
production route was used, and the emissions embedded in it, split into direct
and indirect. You also report any carbon price you already paid in the country
where the goods were made.

Q4 Which emissions do we have to report for steel
During the transitional period, direct emissions only. Indirect emissions are
reported for cement, fertilisers and electricity. Iron and steel, aluminium and
hydrogen are direct only during that period. This is one of the most common
sources of over-reporting.
